history.summary: The Sri Kalimatha Temple, popularly known as the Kali Temple of Visakhapatnam, stands on Beach Road at R.K. Beach, Paanduranga Puram. Dedicated to Goddess Kali, the fierce form of Parvati, it is the city's best-known Kali shrine and a major spiritual and tourist landmark. The temple's architecture is inspired by the Dakshineswar Kali temple near Kolkata, with a central hall and a resplendent idol of Kali adorned in gold and silver ornaments; the complex also houses shrines of Lord Shiva and Lord Ganesha. Sources consistently date its construction to 1984. It is closely associated with Vizag's Bengali community: the Waltair Kalibari (the historic Bengali community temple at Railway New Colony) holds community celebrations here, including the Poila Baisakh Prabhat Pheri that starts from this temple along Beach Road. Durga Puja in September-October draws thousands of devotees to the temple, which overlooks the Bay of Bengal.

town_description: Visakhapatnam (Vizag), the 'City of Destiny', is the largest city of Andhra Pradesh and a major port on the Coromandel Coast of the Bay of Bengal. Known for its beaches - Ramakrishna Beach (R.K. Beach) being the most famous - the submarine museum, Kailasagiri hill and Araku valley nearby, it blends industry, tourism and a rich multi-ethnic community life, including a large Bengali and Odia population dating to the railway and steel plant eras.

travel.airport: Visakhapatnam International Airport (VTZ) (approx. 18 km; taxis and app cabs available).
travel.railway: Visakhapatnam Railway Station (approx. 5 km; buses, autos and taxis available).
travel.road: On Beach Road at R.K. Beach, Paanduranga Puram (530003). Nearest bus stop is Appughar (approx. 500 m); RTC Complex (approx. 5 km). Easily reachable by city buses, auto-rickshaws and taxis.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant coastal weather; September-October is the most vibrant time, during the grand Durga Puja celebrations. Evenings are pleasant year-round with the sea breeze.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Morning 6:00 AM to 12:00 noon; evening 4:00 PM to 8:00 PM, open all days (verify - one source lists closure on Mondays). No entry fee; footwear not allowed inside; photography restrictions apply inside the premises.
